title: The Pipeline Setup Checklist: Fill the Top Every Day So Deals Keep Coming
description: Your pipeline isn't slow, it's empty. The 3-step setup checklist to fill the top every day: a list that fits, inboxes that land, daily volume you track.
lead: This is the full setup checklist from the reel. You get the 3-step checklist (a list of people who fit, a setup that lands in the inbox, volume every day), the math for your daily number, a tank tracker you can paste into Google Sheets, a worked example, a problem finder and a prompt that plans it all for you.
insider: On every client campaign we watch the top of the tank daily: new people in, emails out, bounces, replies. In one full quarter of steady sending from January to March, **236,545 emails brought 4,372 replies and 1,061 interested leads**, because the top never ran dry. The checklist is the easy part; the full system (list, inboxes, follow-ups) is what we do for clients.

blocks.text: The short answer
A slow pipeline has deals in it that move slowly. An **empty** pipeline has nothing in it, because nothing went in. If 0 goes in the top, 0 comes out the bottom. No sales trick fixes that.
Here's what a full tank looked like in the campaign in the reel: one client, one real month.

blocks.text: Why the top decides everything

**There's a delay.** What you put in today turns into replies over the next days and weeks. [Instantly's 2026 benchmark report](https://instantly.ai/cold-email-benchmark-report-2026) found **58% of replies come from the first email and 42% from follow-ups**, and it suggests spacing follow-ups **3 to 4 days apart**. So a 3-email sequence takes about a week to finish for each person. If you skip a week of filling the top, you don't feel it that week. You feel it later, when the calendar is suddenly empty.

**Steady beats bursts.** Instantly found teams that keep sending consistently see **15 to 20% more replies**, and warns that sending 500 on Monday, nothing for three days, then 1,000 on Friday looks suspicious to email providers. [Google's sender guidelines](https://support.google.com/mail/answer/81126) say the same thing: send at a consistent rate and avoid bursts.
The setup checklist
Three steps, the same three from the reel. Each has the why, then exactly how.
Step 1: A list of people who fit

**Why:** volume only helps if it reaches buyers. [Hunter's State of Email Outreach 2026](https://hunter.io/the-state-of-cold-email) found **61% of decision makers** say cold emails fail because they aren't relevant. A full tank of the wrong people is still empty where it counts.

items: Write your fit rules: industry, company size, location, buyer job title, and one sign they need you now.
Contact **1 or 2 people per company**. Hunter found that got a **5.1% reply rate vs 3.5%** for 3 or more.
Verify every email before it goes in. Instantly says to keep bounces **under 2%**.
Build next month's list before this one runs out (our [lead fuel calculator](/guides/fuel.html) gives you the date).
Split the list into small segments with their own first line. Hunter found groups of 21 to 50 people got **6.2% replies vs 2.4%** for 500+.

blocks.text: Step 2: A setup that lands in the inbox

**Why:** an email in spam is an email that never went in. Gmail and Outlook both have hard rules now. Google requires anyone sending **5,000+ emails a day to Gmail** to use SPF, DKIM and DMARC and to keep the spam rate in Postmaster Tools **below 0.3%**. Since May 5, 2025, [Microsoft requires the same three records](https://techcommunity.microsoft.com/blog/microsoftthreatprotectionblog/strengthening-email-ecosystem-outlook%E2%80%99s-new-requirements-for-high%E2%80%90volume-senders/4399730) for domains sending over 5,000 emails a day to Outlook.com, and mail that fails can be rejected.

items: Send from **separate domains** that look like your brand, never your main domain. Hunter found a custom domain got **5.2% replies vs 2.5%** for free Gmail-style addresses.
Add **SPF, DKIM and DMARC** to every sending domain, even if you're far below 5,000 a day.
**Warm up** new inboxes. Instantly suggests starting at 5 to 10 emails a day and building up over **4 to 6 weeks**.
Keep each inbox to about **30 cold emails a day**. Hunter found 20 to 49 a day per inbox got a **5.7% reply rate**, above the 4.5% average.
Connect [Google Postmaster Tools](https://postmaster.google.com) and keep the spam rate under 0.1%, as Google recommends.

blocks.text: Step 3: Volume, every day

**Why:** a tank fills a little every day, not once a month. Steady daily sending gets more replies (Instantly) and builds trust with email providers (Google). It also means replies, calls and deals arrive steadily instead of in feast-or-famine waves.

items: Set your **daily number**: new people in and emails out per day (see the math below).
Set the same sending window in your tool every working day, and cap each inbox at its daily limit.
Load enough verified people for at least **2 weeks** ahead, so a late list never stops the flow.
Fill in the tank tracker every day. It takes 2 minutes.
Answer every reply the same day. A full tank with slow replies leaks at the bottom.

blocks.text: Work out your daily number

items: **Deals you want per month.**
**Emails per deal.** Use your own if you have it. If not, use a careful guess and replace it after your first full month (our [funnel math sheet](/guides/funnel.html) shows how to build one).
**Emails per month** = deals × emails per deal.
**Emails per day** = emails per month ÷ 22 working days.
**New people per day** = emails per day ÷ emails in your sequence.
**Inboxes** = emails per day ÷ 30. Our [sending calculator](/guides/math.html) covers the domains and warm-up.

blocks.text: Worked example
Say you want **5 deals a month** and you borrow the ratio from the campaign in the reel, about 2,288 emails per deal. Your sequence has 3 emails.

Now see what one missed week costs. Five working days without new people is about **870 people** (174 × 5) who never enter, and about **2,610 emails** (870 × 3) never sent. At about 2,288 emails per deal, that's **about 1 deal** that never happens. You'd notice it weeks later, not that week.

blocks.label: Your ratio will be different
blocks.text: 2,288 emails per deal came from one client in one month. In our construction software case, 162,073 emails led to 6 annual contracts, about 27,000 emails per contract. Bigger, slower deals need a much bigger tank. Use your own number as soon as you have it.
The tank tracker
One row per working day. Open a blank Google Sheet, click cell A1 and paste this. Then copy row 2 down for each new day and fill in the numbers.

blocks.label: Copy, then paste into cell A1
blocks.text:
Date	New people in	Emails sent	Bounces	Bounce rate	Replies	Interested	Calls booked	People left in list	Days of list left
2026-11-23	174	520		=IFERROR(D2/C2,0)				2000	=IFERROR(I2/B2,0)

Format column E as a percent. Column J tells you how many working days of new people you have left. In the example row, 2,000 people ÷ 174 a day = about 11.5 days. When it drops under 10, build the next list today.

blocks.text: Common mistakes

items: **Calling an empty pipeline "slow".** If nothing went in this month, waiting won't help.
**Filling the top only when sales are down.** By then you're weeks behind.
**More volume from the same few inboxes.** Push past about 30 a day each and you trade the tank for the spam folder.
**Counting emails, not people.** Follow-ups don't fill the tank. New people do.
**No tracker.** If you don't write down what goes in, you won't see the gap until the calendar is empty.

blocks.text: Plan your daily number with Claude

blocks.label: Tank planner prompt
blocks.text:
Act as my cold email pipeline planner.

Deals I want per month: [number]
Emails per deal: [my number, or "unknown"]
Emails in my sequence: [number]
Working days per month: 22
Inboxes I have now (warmed up): [number]
Verified people left in my list: [number]

Do this:
1) If emails per deal is unknown, ask me for my reply rate, interested rate, call rate and close rate, and calculate it.
2) Calculate emails per month, emails per working day, new people per day and new people per month.
3) Calculate inboxes needed at 30 emails per inbox per day, and how many more I need to add and warm up (4 to 6 weeks).
4) Calculate how many working days my list lasts and the date I must start building the next one.
5) Show what one missed week of new people costs me in deals.
Show everything in tables. Round people and inboxes up.

blocks.label: The rule
blocks.text: Fill the top every day. The bottom takes care of itself.

faq.q: How long until a full tank turns into calls?
faq.a: If your inboxes are already warmed up, replies start in the first days and keep coming as follow-ups go out. If you're starting from zero, add 4 to 6 weeks of warm-up first, as Instantly suggests. That's why you fill the top before you need the calls.

faq.q: Do I really need to send every single day?
faq.a: Every working day is what matters for most B2B sellers. Hunter found the day of the week didn't move reply rates in its data. What hurts is stopping and starting, so pick a daily number you can keep.

faq.q: I don't know my emails per deal. What do I use?
faq.a: Start with a careful guess from our [funnel math sheet](/guides/funnel.html), send for a full month, then replace the guess with your real number. Don't copy the reel's 2,288 blindly; it came from one client.

No. More right-fit people is better. More of the wrong people, or more emails from the same few inboxes, only adds bounces and spam risk. Grow the tank by adding verified people and warmed inboxes together.
